transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I guess… I’ve just been feeling really wound up most of the day. Like my body’s bracing for something, even if I’m just sitting at my computer or trying to relax after dinner.
Do you get sudden episodes of intense fear or discomfort that peak within minutes?
I don’t think so… not like that. I feel tense a lot, but I can’t say it suddenly peaks within minutes or anything.
Does it feel hard to control the worrying?

Yeah… somewhat. I’ll tell myself, “Daniela, enough, just focus on the report,” but then one little thought turns into several, and I end up checking messages or going over what might go wrong for… longer than I meant to. Maybe half an hour sometimes.
Do you find yourself worrying about a lot of different parts of your life, rather than just one specific problem?

Yes… it’s not just one thing. My mind kind of jumps around—my sister in Arecibo, something I might’ve missed at work, my husband driving home, church things, bills. I end up trying to plan for problems that haven’t even happened.
Have you been feeling this way most days for at least six months?
Yes… most days, I think. It’s been about thirteen months now, since my sister in Arecibo started needing a lot more help from us.
Do you get tired easily?
I’m not sure… not especially. I mean, I get tired sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed it being easy or unusual.
Have you been feeling restless, keyed up, or on edge?
Yes… I do. I feel kind of wound up most of the day, like my body is bracing for something. Even if I’m just sitting at my computer, or trying to relax after dinner, I still feel on edge.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?
I don’t think so… not in any way that really stands out. I can usually get through my work.
Have you been more irritable than usual?

A little, yes. I’m usually pretty patient, but lately small things get to me more… like a meeting running late, or too many questions when I’m trying to cook. I don’t mean to, but I answer more sharply than I should.
Have you been having muscle tension?
Yes… I think so. It’s like my body stays tight, like I’m bracing for something, even when I’m just sitting at my computer or trying to relax.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yes… somewhat. I usually fall asleep eventually, but I’ve been waking up around three or four and then my mind starts going—my sister’s appointment, something at work. Even if I’ve technically slept enough, I don’t really feel rested in the morning.
Is this worry causing problems in your daily life?

Some, yes. I’m still getting things done… work, family, church and all that. But reports take me longer because I keep checking them, and I guess I’ve been a little short with people. I’ve had to apologize a few times.
Do you feel that most of this anxiety started because of your sister needing more help?
Yes… I think that’s when it really started. It’s been about thirteen months, since my sister in Arecibo started needing a lot more help from us.
If your sister’s situation were resolved, do you think this anxiety would mostly go away?

I don’t know if it would all go away. I think it would help, yes… but my mind tends to move on to the next thing. Work, my husband getting home safely, bills, church things. I catch myself getting ready for problems that haven’t even happened.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?
Not really… I mean, I get tired and worried, but I wouldn’t say depressed. At least, not that I’ve noticed.
Aside from your sister’s situation, would you still be this anxious?

Probably, yes… maybe not as much, but yes. My mind just keeps moving from one thing to another—work, my husband driving home, bills, church things. I start preparing for problems that haven’t even happened.
Do you feel that your worrying is excessive?
Yes… I think so. It feels like my mind keeps going from one concern to another—my sister, work, my husband driving home, bills. I’ll be preparing for things that haven’t even happened yet.
